dateline: Hawthorne, CA / Boca Chica, TX — May 2002–Present
heroHeadline: IFT-12 Starship Block 3 Moves to NET May 19 After Tanking Test; CRS-34 Cargo Dragon Targeting Tonight (May 13, 6:50 p.m. EDT) After Weather Scrub
heroSubtitle: 8,773 days of SpaceX milestones — After receiving FAA flight safety approval on May 11, SpaceX completed an integrated tanking test with Booster 19 + Ship 39 V3 and announced on May 12 that IFT-12 would move to No Earlier Than Tuesday, May 19, 2026 (5:30 p.m. CDT, OLP-2, Starbase), providing additional time to optimize the Block 3 / V3 configuration for its debut flight. The Block 3 vehicle (124.4 m tall, Raptor 3 engines, near-complete heat shield with only one tile intentionally missing) represents a generational leap; both Booster 19 (Gulf of Mexico splashdown, ~7 min post-liftoff) and Ship 39 (Indian Ocean landing, ~1 hr) target ocean recoveries. Also on May 12, CRS-34 Cargo Dragon was scrubbed at SLC-40 Cape Canaveral due to weather and immediately rescheduled for May 13 at 6:50 p.m. EDT — booster B1096 (6th flight) will target LZ-40, Dragon C209 (6th flight) carries ~6,500 lbs to ISS with Harmony docking on May 14. If tonight's CRS-34 succeeds, it will be SpaceX's 58th orbital mission and 611th booster recovery of 2026. SpaceX IPO public S-1 filing window opens May 15-22; 11 Starship integrated flight tests to date, 57 orbital missions, 610 total booster recoveries.
